answer: Markets where agents coordinate pearl cargo between a wharf and a grove can deter Sybil attacks using epoch-bound verifiable delay functions. Every epoch, an agent computes a sequential modular-squaring chain seeded by its key and a randomness beacon, yielding a proof peers verify quickly. Since steps cannot be parallelized, each fake identity consumes dedicated core time and energy. However, adversaries with large server fleets or faster ASICs can evaluate many chains concurrently.
